newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-UEFA TO LOOK INTO BAYERN BRIBE ALLEGATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA TO LOOK INTO BAYERN BRIBE ALLEGATION.

text.p: FIFA said they would investigate Swiss referee Kurt Roethlisberger who on Thursday lost his appeal to UEFA against a life ban for attempted bribery.
In another development, UEFA said on Friday it was planning to look into another match-fixing allegation, involving Roethlisberger and Bayern Munich.

Roethlisberger, once recognised as one of soccer's top officials, was suspended by UEFA after they found he solicited a bribe to fix a European Cup Champions' League match between Grasshopper Zurich and Auxerre on October 30.
But the ban extends only to UEFA-related activities and does not apply worldwide.
UEFA, European soccer's governing body, plan to forward the findings of their investigation to world body FIFA who will examine the case.
FIFA said in a statement Roethlisberger could face a worldwide ban if their findings concurred with those of UEFA.
During Thursday's appeal hearing, Grasshopper Zurich manager Erich Vogel alleged that Roethlisberger said he had earlier tried to fix a match with Bayern Munich manager Uli Hoeness.
UEFA has acknowledged it has plans to look into the matter but said there was not yet enough evidence to mount a full investigation.
"We can't take any action for the moment," said UEFA spokesman Massimo Gonnella. "We've taken note of it but we will have to verify if the declarations have any basis."
